report_title: Final commitment: exact reduction and pairwise strengthening
nine_line_binding: tools/prepare_test82.py:7 does 'from prepare_test81 import main' and :9 does 'main(82)': the smallest generator in the corpus writes no proof content, no constant and no data of its own, yet cases/test82/proof.rpa is 24,094,089 B. The reason is that the certificate is a function of the instance, not of the file. The work is done by the imported ops: (a) tools/prepare_test88.py:18 Builder (alloc:22, refexpr:24, kind:30, lin:35, eqpair:44, cases:52) owns fact numbering and the Lin/EqPair/Cases step shapes - it is imported by 6 of the 10 modules in the closure; (b) tools/prepare_test70.py:14 SparseBuilder (lin:16) and :32 cases_le_shared own the sparse exact accumulator and the two-branch template; (c) tools/prepare_affine.py:20 parse_mps / :77 row_ref and tools/prepare_test40.py:72-87 expression/plus/mul/expr_json/substitute/row_fact own exact rational readback and algebra; (d) the loop in tools/prepare_test81.py:84-134 recognizes the pair-row family by coefficient shape (4 terms -1/+1/-60000/a_ij, :100-113) and instantiates the templates once per handled row (4,107) and once per obligation (140,914). Reuse reach: 9 lines pull in a 10-module, 1,517-line closure (prepare_test81 187 + prepare_affine 233 + prepare_test40 207 + prepare_test70 149 + prepare_test88 233 + prepare_test19 155 + prepare_test71 126 + prepare_test84 115 + prepare_test57 103). The residual per-instance information is exactly four hardcoded ternaries inside the shared generator: len(removed)==(3341 if case==81 else 3315) (:47), len(tight)==(762 if case==81 else 792) (:88), dependent_equality_deletions=int(case==82) (:150), version=6 if case==81 else 5 (:159). Boundary conclusion: today the reusable unit is a whole case generator imported by name, and the API boundary sits at the MODEL INSTANCE - compile(source.mcm, target.mcm, finding) -> certificate - not at the proof bytes. Evidence that this boundary is real: test82 and test81 differ in only 21 MPS lines (2 header/NAME + 19 RHS values; same 11,090/4,630 structure), which moves the forced-zero count from 3,341 to 3,315 and the rewritten-row count from 762 to 792, i.e. every number in the proof is instance data.

Whole-tree step census: 85,180 Lin, 4,107 Cases, 3,315 EqPair, 3,315 Absurd branch ends, 4,899 Witness branch ends; Lin term-count histogram 53,540 x 1-ref, 8,214 x 2-ref, 9,006 x 3-ref, 4,107 x 104-ref, 6,630 x 0-ref.

Only two Cases shapes for 4,107 records: {kind:Eq, expression 1 term} x3,315 (zero-arc fixing) and {kind:Le, expression 3 terms} x792 (rewritten pair rows), both emitted by the same template (tools/prepare_test70.py:32).
Byte concentration in one family: the 4,107 packing Lins (Lin{Le, constant '0', 1 RowEq + 103 VarLower}) are 10,525,827 B = 43.7% of the RPA; the 3,315 Cases:Eq records are 2,057,119 B = 8.5%.

agent_manual_work: Wrote the entire exact model reader in eval code - a 44,773-line parser with Fraction from decimal strings, explicit section/marker/bound validation and hard failure on unsupported records - with 'framework members touched in eval code: none' (digest transcript).

Discovered the structure by hand: bipartite colouring of the 210 equalities into K105,105, the 4,160 ordered-pair rows found by coefficient pattern (-1/+1/60000/a_ij), p_ij range 33,210.389..49,113.515, 130 singleton windows for the 65 t_i.

Rejected two hypotheses with exact evidence: constant pair parameter (falsified by c276/c277) and 'diagonal one forces a global minimum' - the latter caught by an independent smoke exercise (c741, d=1, X_ij=0, difference -7713), discarding all 51 proposed diagonal fixings (report section 3).

Built the whole verification itself: a second streaming MPS reader for the emitted artifact, 210 retained rows compared after zero substitution, 9,165 allowed-state threshold identities, 38,244 deterministic smoke cases, 2,601,532 B audit.json with per-record witnesses and both SHA-256 hashes.

Hand-measured every fact the proof needs: the 3,315 forced-zero arcs (U_j-L_i < a_ij checked exactly), the 3,368 removable pair rows, the 792 rewritten rows with new coefficient a_ij-D_ij, and the c209 identity sum(A)-sum(B)=0 over 11,025 variables.

friction: The finding is not an input: prepare() receives the agent's audit.json (2,601,532 B of exact witnesses) but dereferences it only under 'if case==81' (:136-145); test82 re-derives all 3,315 zero-arc witnesses, the 792 rewritten rows and the c209 dependency from the two models alone (:43, :100-113).

The 24 MB is emitted element by element: 4,107 packing Lins (10.5 MB), 4,107 Cases records with 2 distinct shapes, 140,914 obligation refs; docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:380-381 states shared affine-expression/mapping DAGs and dedicated batch records are not implemented by this wire layout, against a 256 MiB RPA text cap (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:390).
Byte-bound, not work-bound: 24,094,089 B of RPA for work 4,533,178 = 0.45% of the default budget, and the generator only learns the size after encode() writes the file (tools/prepare_test81.py:160).

Negative checks are hand-scripted dict surgery on the generator's own output: pop one term from cert['blocks'][0]['steps'][0]['Lin']['terms'] (or a branch term, or a check ref), re-encode, reassemble, re-verify a 17 MB RPX, three times (tools/prepare_test81.py:173-180; cases/test82/preparation.json negative_checks).

Reuse is at file granularity, not fact granularity: the 9-line file imports a sibling case's main() because no named reusable certificate facts exist, so the identical-structure test81 needs the same generator and differs only in four ternaries (:47, :88, :150, :159).
top_capability: RULE_BUILDERS (the duplicated integer-case/Lin step machinery that generated the 23 MB), with BATCH_TEMPLATES as its byte-side consequence.
notes: All facts measured on cases/test82 (preparation.json status VERIFIED, 4 kernel runs exit 0, rpa_bytes 24,094,089) and on the digest transcript. The 9-line generator is the corpus's clearest demonstration that proof construction here is a pure function of the model instance plus an edit list: the same 187-line shared generator serves two instances that differ in 19 RHS values, and the only per-instance code is four ternaries. Consequence for the compiler: the API must expose the instance (readback + instance-parameterised rule builders) and the edit list, and must stop treating the proof text as the hand-authored artifact.
